record.title: Independence-number rationality conjecture for FI-graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{\bullet}$ be an $\operatorname{FI}$-graph, and let $\alpha(G_n)$ denote its independence number. Define the generating function

$$
\sum_{n \geq 0} \alpha(G_n)t^n.
$$

**Independence-number rationality conjecture.** The generating function is rational. In particular, the function $n \mapsto \alpha(G_n)$ agrees with a quasi-polynomial for all $n \gg 0$.

This conjecture asks whether the extremal invariant given by independence numbers exhibits the same eventual regularity as counting invariants of $\operatorname{FI}$-graphs. The paper provides experimental evidence, including a classification of $\operatorname{FI}$-graphs with quadratically growing vertex sets, but no resolution is stated.
record.source_name: David Guan and Eric Ramos, “Independence numbers in certain families of highly symmetric graphs”, arXiv:2401.16739 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16739

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: The min-plus dot product dimension is bounded by the max-plus dot product dimension
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\rho_{_{_T}}(G)$ for its min-plus dot product dimension and $\rho_{_{\widehat{T}}}(G)$ for its max-plus dot product dimension.

**Dimension inequality.**

$$
\rho_{_{_T}}(G) \leq \rho_{_{\widehat{T}}}(G)
$$

for all graphs $G$.

The preceding example shows that the two dimensions need not be equal, while the paper establishes that the ordinary dot product dimension is a lower bound for the max-plus dimension. Thus this is the remaining possible uniform bounding relationship between the min-plus and max-plus dot product dimensions; its status is not determined in the source.
record.source_name: Sean Bailey, David Brown, Michael Snyder and Nicole Turner, “Dot Product Representations of Graphs Using Tropical Arithmetic”, arXiv:2402.14953 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14953

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Surjectivity conjecture for higher pages of cyclic equivariant slice spectral sequences
record.statement:
For $m,n\geq 1$, let

$$
\operatorname{SliceSS}(BP^{(C_{2^n})}\langle m+1\rangle)\longrightarrow \operatorname{SliceSS}(BP^{(C_{2^n})}\langle m\rangle)
$$

be the map of slice spectral sequences induced by the quotient map. Write $\mathcal{E}_r$ for the $r$-th page and $d_r$ for its differential.

**Surjectivity conjecture.** For all $m\geq 1$ and $r\geq 2$, this map induces a surjection on the $\mathcal{E}_r$-page and on the $d_r$-differentials.

Surjectivity on the $\mathcal{E}_2$-page is known and is suggested as a route toward proving the height classification conjecture. Surjectivity on every higher page and for the corresponding differentials is not established in the supplied context.
record.source_name: Lennart Meier, XiaoLin Danny Shi and Mingcong Zeng, “Transchromatic phenomena in the equivariant slice spectral sequence”, arXiv:2403.00741 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00741

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2024). “In addition to the transchromatic phenomenon proved in , the following conjecture offers another transchromatic approach to studying the $\Cn$-fixed points of $E_h$ across different heights:”

record.title: Folsom–Homma–Ryu–Tong congruence conjecture for $M$-ary partitions
record.statement:
Let $M=(m_j)_{j=0}^{8}$ be a sequence of integers and let $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_j)_{j=1}^{r-1}\in\{0,1\}^{r-1}$ be fixed. Let $p_M(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into parts $m_0m_1\cdots m_s$, and define

$$
\mu_j=\frac{m_j}{\gcd(m_j,P_j)},\qquad \sigma=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}\varepsilon_j\prod_{i=0}^{j}m_i,
$$

where $P_j=\prod_{p\leq j}p$ is the product of all primes up to $j$. Then

**Folsom–Homma–Ryu–Tong conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq1$ and $0\leq c\leq m_1-1$,

$$
p_M(m_1\cdots m_r n-\sigma-m_1-c)\equiv0\pmod{\mu_1\cdots\mu_r}.
$$

This conjecture was posed by Folsom, Homma, Ryu, and Tong as a proposed generalization of congruences for ordinary $m$-ary partitions. The supplied text does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Błażej Żmija, “High order congruences for M-ary partitions”, arXiv:2403.04495 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04495

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Propp's quotient conjecture for $(3n+1,3n+1)$-benzels
record.statement:
Let $T_n$ denote the number of stones-and-bones tilings of the $(3n+1,3n+1)$-benzel in which the vertical bone is forbidden.

**Propp's conjecture.** The numbers $T_n$ satisfy

$$
\frac{T_n}{T_{n-1}}=\frac{2^{2n}(4n-1)!(4n-2)!n!}{(3n)!(3n-1)!(3n-2)!}
$$

for all $n\geq 2$. This replaces Propp's original Problem 9 with a more precise conjecture, supported by additional data obtained through the perfect-matching formulation and Kasteleyn's determinant method; it remains open.
record.source_name: Colin Defant, Leigh Foster, Rupert Li, James Propp and Benjamin Young, “Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression”, arXiv:2403.07663 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07663

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: The additive-map factorization conjecture for alternative division rings
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an alternative division ring, and let $f,g:D\rightarrow D$ be additive maps. For every $x\in D^\times$, where $D^\times$ denotes the set of invertible elements of $D$, suppose that

$$
f(x)+x^2g(x^{-1})=0.
$$

**Additive-map factorization conjecture.** There exists a fixed element $q\in D$ such that

$$
f(x)=xq\qquad\text{and}\qquad g(x)=-xq
$$

for all $x\in D$. This conjecture concerns the common structure of additive solutions to an inverse functional equation in alternative division rings; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Daniel Kawai and Bruno Leonardo Macedo Ferreira, “Unraveling Functional Equations in Composition Algebra: Resolving Conjectures and Examining Implications”, arXiv:2403.17971 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17971

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Bounded neighborhoods in K4-free, induced-path-free signed graphs
record.statement:
For a signed graph $\widehat{G}$ and a vertex $u$, let $N[u]$ denote the closed neighborhood of $u$, and let $\chi_b$ denote balanced chromatic number. **Bounded-neighborhood conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists a positive integer $b_k$ such that, whenever

$$
\widehat{G}\in\operatorname{Forb}_{ind}(\{\widehat{(K_4,-)},P_k\}),
$$

every vertex $u$ of $\widehat{G}$ has closed neighborhood satisfying

$$
\chi_b(N[u])\leq b_k.
$$

This conjecture is presented as an equivalent relaxation of the conjecture for arbitrary linear forests: the paper proves that such a neighborhood bound yields a global balanced-coloring bound. It remains open.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Allen Ibiapina, Luis Kuffner, Reza Naserasr, Cyril Pujol, Cléophée Robin and Huan Zhou, “Extension of the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture to signed graphs”, arXiv:2511.03335 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Equivalent local boundedness conjecture for signed graph classes
record.statement:
Let $(K_3,-)$ denote the signed triangle with the specified signature, let $(K_4,M)$ denote the signed complete graph whose negative edges form a matching of size two, and let $P_k$ be a path on the conventionally specified number of vertices. **Equivalent local boundedness conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists a positive integer $b_k$ such that every signed graph in

$$
\operatorname{Forb}_{ind}(\{(K_3,-),(K_4,M),P_k\})
$$

has balanced chromatic number at most $b_k$.

The paper gives this as a reformulation of the bounded-neighborhood conjecture, using switching and the structure of the neighborhood of a vertex. It remains open.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Allen Ibiapina, Luis Kuffner, Reza Naserasr, Cyril Pujol, Cléophée Robin and Huan Zhou, “Extension of the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture to signed graphs”, arXiv:2511.03335 (2025).

record.title: The most general divisor-set conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let divisibility of a product mean that each integer in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ divides that product. **The most general divisor-set conjecture.** For every $n$, there exists a set $S$ of size $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/3})$, with each $s\in S$ of size $\widetilde{O}(n^{n^{1/3}})$, such that

$$
1,\ldots,n\mid\prod_{s,t\in S}(s-t).
$$

The paper presents this as a more general variation of the preceding structured conjectures, while noting that it is not currently known how to turn it into algorithms. No resolution evidence is supplied.
record.source_name: Chris Umans and Siki Wang, “A number-theoretic conjecture implying faster algorithms for polynomial factorization and integer factorization”, arXiv:2511.10851 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10851

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Conjecture on the Steiner diameter and Steiner (k,k')-radius of trees
record.statement:
Let $n$, $k$, and $k^{\prime}$ be integers with $n\geq k\geq3$ and $k>k^{\prime}\geq1$, and let $T$ be a tree with order $n$. **The Steiner diameter–radius conjecture.**

$$
Sd_k(T)\leq\frac{k}{k-k^{\prime}}Sr_{k,k^{\prime}}(T)-\frac{k^{\prime}(k^{\prime}-1)}{k-k^{\prime}}.
$$

The paper proves the inequality for $k^{\prime}=2$ and $k^{\prime}=3$, and states that it generalizes the known result for $k^{\prime}=1$. Its validity for all $k^{\prime}\geq1$ under the displayed hypotheses remains open.
record.source_name: Qingnan Zhang and Yingzhi Tian, “On the Steiner k-diameter and Steiner (k,k^)-radius of trees”, arXiv:2511.22492 (2025).
record.references:

record.title: The square-free word conjecture for sequences of ternary-or-larger alphabets
record.statement:
An **alphabet** is a finite set. Let $(\mathcal{A}_i)_{i\ge1}$ be a sequence of alphabets, and say that a word $w=w_1\ldots w_n$ **respects** this sequence when $w_i\in\mathcal{A}_i$ for every $i$. A word is **square-free** if it contains no factor of the form $uu$ for a nonempty word $u$.

**Square-free word conjecture.** Given a sequence of alphabets $(\mathcal{A}_i)_{i\ge1}$ with $|\mathcal{A}_i|\ge3$ for all $i$, there exists an infinite square-free word that respects $(\mathcal{A}_i)_{i\ge1}$.

The source states this as a reformulation of the Thue list-number conjecture for the infinite path. It is presented as an open conjectural formulation, while the paper's main result concerns the analogous existence theorem for binary alphabets and cube-free words.
record.source_name: Vuong Bui and Matthieu Rosenfeld, “There exist infinite cube-free words over any sequence of binary alphabets”, arXiv:2512.03670 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: The conjecture on polynomial-size join/union expressions for permutation cycles
record.statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathfrak{C}_n$ be the set of $n$-cycles in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. A join/union expression is an expression built using the paper's join and union operations that represents a set of maps. **Cycle-expression conjecture.** For every polynomial $P$, there exists an integer $n$ such that $\mathfrak{C}_n$ does not have a join/union expression of size at most $P(n)$, even if $n$ is represented in unary. The preceding theorem gives a conditional obstruction: a polynomial-time construction would imply ${\sf P}={\sf NP}$. The source presents the unconditional size lower bound as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Ambroise Baril, Miguel Couceiro and Victor Lagerkvist, “New Perspectives on Semiring Applications to Dynamic Programming”, arXiv:2512.03916 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03916

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “We view it as an interesting open question to prove this unconditionally and pose the following conjecture.”

record.title: Barnette's conjecture on simple separating non-contractible cycles
record.statement:
A **simple separating non-contractible cycle** (SNCC) is a simple cycle in a triangulation that is both separating and non-contractible. Let $t$ be an arbitrary triangulation without loops or multiple edges, of genus at least $2$. **Barnette's conjecture.** The triangulation $t$ contains a simple SNCC.

This is a longstanding deterministic conjecture, despite several advances. It asks whether every such triangulation has a simple separating non-contractible cycle; the paper notes that the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Baptiste Louf, “The separating systole and the genus ratio of high genus triangulations”, arXiv:2512.05068 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05068

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Beck–Fiala discrepancy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a hypergraph on a finite ground set $X$, where every vertex has degree at most $d$. **Beck–Fiala's conjecture.** There exists a function $f:X\rightarrow\{-1,1\}$ such that for every $e\in\mathcal H$,

$$
\left|\sum_{x\in e}f(x)\right|\leqslant C\sqrt d,
$$

where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. The source describes this as the hypergraph-colouring companion to Komlós's conjecture and notes that Komlós's conjecture implies it; it is presented as open.
record.source_name: Julian Sahasrabudhe, “Probabilistic combinatorics at exponentially small scales”, arXiv:2512.15077 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15077

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Sparse triangle-free diameter-two graph conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A graph is **triangle-free** if it contains no triangle, and has **diameter $2$** if every two vertices are at distance at most $2$. **Sparse triangle-free diameter-two graph conjecture.** For every integer $t\geqslant2$, there exists an integer $n_0$ such that if $G$ is a triangle-free diameter-$2$ graph that does not contain $K_{2,t}$ as a subgraph and has $n\geqslant n_0$ vertices, then $G$ is the star graph $K_{1,n-1}$. The conjecture is attributed in the paper to Wood and is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Jofre Costa, Eric Luu, David R. Wood and Jung Hon Yip, “Verifying Hadwiger's Conjecture for Examples of Graphs with α(G) = 2”, arXiv:2512.17114 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17114

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: The 5-flow reconfiguration conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ denote its reconfiguration graph whose vertices are nowhere-zero $k$-flows, with adjacency given by changing flow values only on a cycle of $G$. A graph is **2-edge-connected** if it has no bridge. **The 5-flow reconfiguration conjecture.** For every 2-edge-connected graph $G$, the reconfiguration graph

$$
\mathcal{F}(G,5)
$$

is connected. This is a reconfiguration analogue of the existence question in Tutte's 5-flow conjecture; unlike existence, connectedness does not imply that the reconfiguration graph is nonempty, and the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Louis Esperet, Kevin Hendrey, Aurélie Lagoutte, Margaux Marseloo, Sergey Norin and Raphael Steiner, “Nowhere-zero flow reconfiguration”, arXiv:2512.17342 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Linear growth conjecture for the paper's sequence-production algorithm
record.statement:
Let $u$ be a forbidden sequence, and let $s(n,u)$ be the sequence produced by the algorithm referenced in the source. **Linear growth conjecture.** The length of $s(n,u)$ grows at most linearly in $n$, for every sequence $u$.

The conjecture is motivated by examples in which the algorithm produces repeating patterns and gives linear bounds for particular forbidden sequences. Whether the algorithm always has this linear-growth property is left open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Shihan Kanungo, “Upper Bounds for Sequence Saturation”, arXiv:2512.17683 (2025).

record.title: Stabilization conjecture for near-perfect powers of colored partition numbers
record.statement:
Let $p_r(n)$ denote the $r$-colored partition function, and define $L_{p_r}(d)$ and $M_{p_r,k}(d)$ analogously to the corresponding quantities for the partition and overpartition functions. **The colored-partition stabilization conjecture.** For each non-negative integer $d$, there is a positive integer $N_d$ such that for all $k\geq N_d$,

$$
M_{p_r,k}(d)=L_{p_r}(d).
$$

The source proposes this as an analogue of the Merca–Ono–Tsai stabilization conjecture and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Summer Haag, Praneel Samanta, Swati, Holly Swisher, Stephanie Treneer and Robin Visser, “Repellent properties of perfect powers on partition functions: a heuristic approach”, arXiv:2601.18138 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2501.03754](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03754).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18138

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “This conjecture has been verified for all $n \leq 10^8$ by Alekseyev , but still remains an open problem.”

record.title: Shen et al.'s homotopy conjecture for total cut complexes of powers of cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_n^r$ denote the $r$th power of the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\Delta_d^t(C_n^r)$ denote its total $d$-cut complex. For $d\geq3$ and $n\geq(2d-1)r+1$, **Shen et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\Delta_d^t(C_n^r)\simeq\mathbb{S}^{n-2d}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is partially resolved: the asserted homotopy equivalence is proved for $r\geq2$ and $n\geq2rd$ for all $d\geq2$, while the full stated range remains unresolved.
record.source_name: Andrés Carnero Bravo, “Total cut complexes and their duals”, arXiv:2602.21427 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2512.04486](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04486).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21427

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

record.title: Kang–Nikiforov–Yuan's explicit spectral-radius conjecture for chromatic hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic $r$-graph of order $n>(r-1)k$, where $k\geq 2$ and $r\geq 4$. For $p\geq 1$, let $\lambda^{(p)}(G)$ denote its $p$-spectral radius. **Kang–Nikiforov–Yuan's explicit conjecture.** For every $p\geq 1$, 
$$
\lambda^{(p)}(G)<r!\left(\binom{n}{r}-k\binom{n/k}{r}\right)n^{-r/p},
$$
 unless $k\mid n$ and $G$ is isomorphic to $Q_k^r(n)$. This is the explicit form of the preceding spectral extremal conjecture; it gives the claimed bound in terms of the number of vertices and is unresolved for general uniformity.
record.source_name: Xizhi Liu and Junchi Luo, “The spectral radius of k-chromatic r-graphs”, arXiv:2605.14755 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2509.24354](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24354).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14755

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).
